leftBlocks.title: Abstract
leftBlocks.content: This paper explores Jensen's Inequality, a cornerstone theorem in convex analysis and probability theory. We provide a clear statement of the theorem along with a proof leveraging convex functions and expectation operators. The inequality's broad applicability spans statistics, economics, and optimization.

slides.title: Jensen's Inequality
slides.lede: Statement of Jensen's Inequality for convex functions and random vectors

leftBlocks.title: Theorem (Jensen's Inequality)
leftBlocks.content:
Let \( F: \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R} \) be convex on convex set \( \mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \), and \( \mathbf{X} \) a random vector with \( \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}] \in \mathcal{X} \). Then:
\[ F\big(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}]\big) \leq \mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{X})]. \]

slides.title: Proof Sketch
slides.lede: Using subgradients and linearity of expectation

leftBlocks.title: Proof Outline
leftBlocks.content:
By convexity, for any \( \mathbf{x}_0 \in \mathcal{X} \), there exists \( \mathbf{g} \in \partial F(\mathbf{x}_0) \) with:
\[ F(\mathbf{x}) \geq F(\mathbf{x}_0) + \langle \mathbf{g}, \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0 \rangle, \quad \forall \mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{X}. \]
Set \( \mathbf{x}_0 = \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}] \) and take expectation:
\[ \mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{X})] \geq F(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}]) + \langle \mathbf{g}, \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}] - \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}] \rangle = F(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}]). \]
